results.name: Basílica de la Sagrada Família
results.why_it_is_special: Designed by Antoni Gaudí and under construction since 1882, it is the largest unfinished Catholic church in the world. Its Nativity Facade and crypt are a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2005), and it was consecrated as a minor basilica in 2010. The interior's tree-like columns and spectacular stained glass are unlike any other church.

results.name: Museu Picasso
results.why_it_is_special: Housed in five medieval Gothic palaces on Carrer de Montcada, the museum holds over 4,200 works and offers the world's most comprehensive collection of Picasso's formative and early years. Highlights include the complete Las Meninas series and Blue Period works. Opened in 1963 at Picasso's own request.

results.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
results.why_it_is_special: Built 1905–1908 by architect Lluís Domènech i Montaner for the Orfeó Català choral society, it is the only Modernista concert hall declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1997). Its steel-framed auditorium is flooded with natural light through extraordinary stained-glass walls and an inverted dome ceiling.

results.name: Casa Batlló
results.why_it_is_special: Radically remodelled by Gaudí between 1904 and 1906, this residential building is known locally as the "House of Bones" for its skeletal façade. Its undulating exterior, colourful broken-tile mosaics (trencadís), and nature-inspired interiors earned it UNESCO World Heritage status in 2005. Now features immersive galleries exploring Gaudí's creative process.

results.name: Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC)
results.why_it_is_special: Housed in the Palau Nacional, a neo-Baroque palace built for the 1929 International Exposition, MNAC holds the world's finest collection of Romanesque mural paintings alongside Gothic, Renaissance, Baroque, and Modernisme galleries. Works by El Greco, Velázquez, Gaudí, Ramon Casas, and Dalí feature in a collection spanning over 1,000 years of Catalan art.
